motivation: The original fixed 9B development prompts have 1,106 common prefix positions among 6,636 positions for two full prefills plus four suffix tokens. Sharing them can avoid 16.67% of these positions before counting truncation of the other donor layers. The full-service candidate cheap-reader run spent about 87% of its time preparing the two states. Retain the working sixteen-step solver and test the largest remaining reusable computation.
inputs: The same eight exposed seeds, table/prose, target/nuisance donors, both written/unwritten. No answer labels enter model execution. Use the original full 16-step method, an exact partial donor, sharing the maximal common prompt prefix plus a partial donor, and joint batch-two prefilling of the full donor and recipient. All use the same fused 16-step readout from identical published code and the same donor/recipient input strings and model revision.
strict_write: Compare the actual 256 donor values byte for byte and the unedited recipient convolution slot against the full reference for every case. Also compare top tokens, per-condition preservation, finite full-logit discrepancies and per-seed cost. A schedule that changes any donor bytes cannot be promoted as a same-write implementation, even if answers match. Count those appearances and the size of the differences. Keep original predictions, including failures. Batching can save latency without saving arithmetic; report those separately.
gate: Promote only on exact donor and original recipient-slot parity, all full-reader target successes and preservation controls, and >=20% lower measured complete time vs the full reader, with mean cost also below the truncated-donor comparator. Report total layer-token accounting and paired bootstrap; do not treat positions as exact FLOPs. No alternative seed or kernel retuning after results.
budget: Ten minutes on local GPU, one engineering repair, no paid credits. This is a screen for additional viable full-service savings before training any predictor.
